answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any delivery disruption is high-cost, and memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters — too risky to switch primary supply now. Memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal has historically recovered real margin (price and terms) without disrupting service, and memory_c1/c6 show incumbent relationships have kept integration stable and multi-year commitments have lowered unit cost. Given the 14-day contract deadline and the finance mandate, negotiating renewed terms with the incumbent addresses the cost target while preserving delivery reliability, deferring the higher-risk second-source or vendor-switch decisions to the next review cycle when there's more slack to absorb transition risk.
